original_question: Let (n_i) be an increasing sequence of positive integers, and suppose there is a prime p such that the power series sum z^{n_i} in F_p[[z]] is algebraic over F_p(z). Must the real number sum 10^{-n_i} be either rational or transcendental?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 5.4 (Loxton and van der Poorten) in §5.2, "Function Fields".
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main objects and arithmetic direction of the paper's statement: an increasing sequence of positive integers, the existence of a prime p, the lacunary formal power series f(z) = ∑_{i>=0} z^{n_i} viewed in F_p[[z]], the hypothesis that f is algebraic over F_p(z), and the transcendence question for the associated real number α = ∑_{i>=0} 10^{-n_i}.
missing_details: The paper states the sequence as (n_i)_{i>=0} and writes both sums explicitly over i>=0.
A crucial hypothesis is missing: the formal power series f(z) = ∑_{i>=0} z^{n_i} must be irrational in the function-field sense, namely f(z) not in F_p(z).
The parenthetical clarification 'irrational (i.e., does not belong to F_p(z))' refers to the formal power series, not to the real number α.
The paper does not ask for the weaker dichotomy 'rational or transcendental'; it asks directly whether α is transcendental under the added hypothesis f(z) not in F_p(z).

The statement belongs specifically to the function-field / automata-theory context of §5.2, so the refined question should keep that scope rather than recast it as a broader decimal-expansion problem.
refined_question: Let (n_i)_{i>=0} be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers. Suppose there exists a prime number p such that the formal power series f(z) = ∑_{i>=0} z^{n_i} in F_p[[z]] is algebraic over F_p(z) and irrational in the sense that f(z) does not belong to F_p(z). Must the real number α = ∑_{i>=0} 10^{-n_i} be transcendental?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: let (n_i)_{i>=0} be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers, and assume that for some prime p the series f(z) = ∑_{i>=0} z^{n_i} lies in F_p[[z]], is algebraic over F_p(z), and satisfies f(z) not in F_p(z). Is the real number ∑_{i>=0} 10^{-n_i} transcendental?
justification: This draft is clearly targeting Conjecture 5.4, because the paper's statement uses exactly the same ingredients: an increasing sequence (n_i), a prime p, the series ∑ z^{n_i} in F_p[[z]], algebraicity over F_p(z), and the decimal number ∑ 10^{-n_i}. In §5.2 Waldschmidt introduces the conjecture as part of the function-field and automata-theoretic transcendence discussion, then states it with one extra hypothesis that your draft omits: the formal series must be 'irrational,' explicitly glossed as 'does not belong to F_p(z)'. Under that hypothesis, the paper asks for transcendence of the real number itself, not merely whether it is 'rational or transcendental.' So your draft is close to the intended target, but it is not fully paper-faithful until that nonrationality hypothesis is restored and the conclusion is sharpened back to pure transcendence.
